mainTopic: Replacing an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמה, how its blood is collected, and what happens to replaced יום הכפורים animals
overview: An אשם מצורע that was slaughtered שלא לשמה still goes on the מזבח, but it does not make the מצורע pure. רבי יוחנן says that whether he can bring a second אשם depends on an argument between רבי מאיר, who starts over, and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, who continue from where they stopped. רב חסדא objects that the פסוק says 'אותו', so no replacement should work for anyone, and the גמרא admits this is a difficulty. A ברייתא saying the מצורע 'needs another אשם' seems to support רבי יוחנן. רב חסדא reads 'needs' as 'he needs one but has no remedy', and the גמרא backs this reading from בית שמאי's ruling about a bald נזיר, as רבי אבינא explains it. רבי פדת disagrees with that reading and compares בית שמאי to רבי אלעזר, who lets the blood go on the spot of a missing thumb. Next, a ברייתא teaches that two כהנים catch the blood of the אשם מצורע: one in his hand for the מצורע, and one in a כלי for the מזבח. The גמרא then returns to יום הכפורים animals whose blood spilled and were replaced, and quotes a dispute over which of them are burned at the בית הדשן. Finally, רבא asks רב נחמן how many goats are sent to עזאזל, and רבא's reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case depends on an earlier argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמה depends on the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר with רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a מצורע's guilt-offering was slaughtered with the wrong intent, we have reached the argument between רבי מאיר on one side and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון on the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן says this case is not new. It fits into an argument we already know. This line sets up the next two steps, which explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם מצורע killed שלא לשמה is still offered on the מזבח, but it does not purify the מצורע. So the question is whether he can bring a second אשם. רבי יוחנן ties this question to a known dispute about what to do when a service was interrupted or done wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt-offering brought by a recovering מצורע; its blood purifies him
Not for its own sake, meaning with intent for a different קרבן
We have reached the argument; this case depends on a known dispute

phrases.english: A leper's guilt-offering that he slaughtered not for its own sake —
we have arrived at the dispute of Rabbi Meir
and Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאנוּ לְמַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's statement from earlier on the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether the מצורע can fix this with a second אשם depends on the רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר / רבי שמעון dispute.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: bring another animal
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, who says you start over from the beginning, the מצורע brings another animal and slaughters it.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר, who said 'he brings another and starts from the beginning,' here too he brings another animal and slaughters it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the first side. רבי מאיר holds that a service that was not finished properly counts as if it never happened, so the מצורע just brings a new אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the wrongly slaughtered אשם counts as nothing for the purification. So nothing stands in the way of bringing a fresh animal and doing the process again.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings another animal
And starts again from the beginning
Here too; the same rule applies in this case

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir, who said
he brings another and starts from the beginning —
here too he brings another and slaughters it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאָמַר יָבִיא אַחֵר וְיַתְחִיל בַּתְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the dispute named in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the מצורע brings a new אשם and slaughters it.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון: no remedy
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, who say you continue from where you stopped, the מצורע has no remedy.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, who say he begins from the place where he stopped, here he has no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the second side. Since these תנאים hold that the first service still counts, a new animal cannot replace it, so the מצורע is stuck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For them the first slaughtering is valid as a step, and you only continue from it. But the blood of this animal cannot purify him, and the תורה wants one אשם, not two. So there is no way forward.

keyTerms.meaning: From the place where he stopped
He has no remedy; there is no way to fix it

steps.confusionAlert: 'No remedy' does not mean the קרבן is thrown out. It is still offered on the מזבח. The problem is only that the מצורע cannot become pure through it, and he cannot bring a replacement either.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon, who say
from the place where he stopped, from there he begins —
here he has no remedy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁאוֹמְרִים מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁפָּסַק מִשָּׁם הוּא מַתְחִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second side of the dispute, in contrast to רבי מאיר in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, the מצורע has no remedy.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the verse says 'it'
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא challenges רבי יוחנן: the פסוק says 'אותו', so even רבי מאיר should agree that a second animal cannot be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objected: But it is written 'אותו' ('it')!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks how רבי יוחנן explained רבי מאיר. He says the פסוק itself requires that same animal, so a replacement is never allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (ויקרא יד:יב) says 'and offer it for a guilt-offering,' meaning the same animal that was waved earlier. If the תורה requires that specific animal, then a new one cannot work, whatever your view on starting over. So according to everyone the מצורע would have no remedy.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to him
'It,' meaning that specific animal
It is written in the פסוק

phrases.english: Rav Chisda strongly objected to it:
But isn't 'it' written?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: וְהָא ״אוֹתוֹ״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבי מאיר half of רבי יוחנן's statement (step 2)
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that, according to רבי מאיר, the מצורע may bring another animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'אותו' requires that same animal, so no replacement can work, even for רבי מאיר.

steps.title: The objection stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רב חסדא's question is a real difficulty for רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives no answer. It simply says רב חסדא's question remains a difficulty for רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'קשיא' alone means the challenge is unresolved, but it does not fully reject רבי יוחנן. That leaves room for the next step to bring support for him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question stands without an answer

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' is weaker than 'תיובתא'. The view is left with an open problem, not fully refuted.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 4 without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא's 'אותו' objection remains an open difficulty for רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמה, or whose blood was not put on the thumbs, goes on the מזבח, but the מצורע needs another אשם. This seems to support רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבי יוחנן: a מצורע's guilt-offering that was slaughtered not for its own sake, or whose blood was not put on the thumbs, is offered on the מזבח and needs נסכים, and he needs another אשם to make him pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to back רבי יוחנן. It says the מצורע 'needs another אשם,' which sounds like a replacement is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the first animal is still a proper קרבן, since it goes on the מזבח with נסכים. But it did not purify the מצורע, so he 'needs another אשם.' That matches רבי יוחנן's statement that, at least according to one view, a second animal works, which goes against רב חסדא's 'אותו' argument.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in agreement with him
Thumbs and big toes, where the blood is placed on the מצורע
Libations of wine, flour and oil brought with the קרבן
To make him fit, meaning to complete his purification

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan:
a leper's guilt-offering that he slaughtered not for its own sake,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן מִדָּמוֹ לְגַבֵּי בְהוֹנוֹת —
phrases.english: or he did not put of its blood on the thumbs —
this goes up on the altar,
and requires libations,
and he needs another guilt-offering to make him fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the difficulty in step 5, brings support for רבי יוחנן
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that a second אשם can be brought (according to רבי מאיר)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating 'וצריך אשם אחר להכשירו'
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the first animal still keeps its status as an אשם and is offered properly, even though it fails to purify the מצורע.

steps.title: רב חסדא's reading: he needs it but has no fix
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא would explain 'צריך' as: he needs another אשם, but he has no way to bring one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא would say to you: what does 'needs' mean? He needs it, and he has no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב חסדא avoids the proof. He reads 'needs another אשם' as describing what is missing, not as permission to bring one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'צריך' could mean 'he may bring another,' or it could mean 'he is lacking another, which he cannot bring.' רב חסדא takes the second reading, so the ברייתא fits his view that 'אותו' blocks any replacement. The proof for רבי יוחנן is therefore not decisive.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you; how this אמורא would answer
What does 'needs' mean?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: the case depends on the רבי מאיר vs. רבי אלעזר / רבי שמעון dispute. רב חסדא: 'אותו' means no replacement for anyone, and the גמרא leaves this as a קשיא. The ברייתא's 'צריך אשם אחר' can be read either way: as permission (רבי יוחנן) or as 'he needs one but cannot bring it' (רב חסדא).

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda would say to you:
what does 'needs' mean —
he needs it, but he has no remedy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר לְךָ: מַאי צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 6 by rereading its key word
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the ברייתא; it does not prove רבי יוחנן wrong
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'צריך' means 'he may bring another,' but it can mean 'he lacks another and has no remedy.'

steps.title: Would a תנא say 'needs' when he means 'no remedy'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב חסדא's reading of the ברייתא. Would a תנא really use the word 'צריך' to mean 'he needs it, but there is no fix'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But would a תנא really teach 'he needs', when he means that he has no remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חסדא's explanation from the last step. It asks whether the word 'צריך' can really mean 'he has no remedy'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, 'he needs another אשם' sounds like 'go bring one'. Reading it as 'he needs one but can never bring one' seems like a stretch. If that reading fails, the ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן again.

keyTerms.meaning: Needs / must
A remedy or fix
A teacher of the משנה or ברייתא period

phrases.english: And would a tanna teach: 'needs'
when he means he has no remedy?
phrases.notes: He's saying this in surprise. It's not really a question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It attacks the דחיה from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's reading of 'צריך' as 'he needs one but has no remedy'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning of 'צריך' is a real obligation that can be carried out. It does not mean a hopeless situation.

steps.title: Yes: the bald נזיר shows 'needs' can mean 'no remedy'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes. It brings the case of a completely bald נזיר. רבי אבינא explains that when בית שמאי say 'צריך' there, they mean he needs it but has no remedy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. A ברייתא teaches about a completely bald נזיר. בית שמאי say he must pass a razor over his head. בית הלל say he does not need to. רבי אבינא said: when בית שמאי say 'must', they mean he must, and since he cannot, he has no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It shows another place where 'צריך' is understood to mean 'he needs it but has no way to do it'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bald נזיר has no hair to shave, so a razor does nothing. רבי אבינא reads בית שמאי as saying the shaving is required and cannot happen, so the נזיר is stuck. This proves the word 'צריך' can carry exactly the meaning רב חסדא gave it.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר who is completely bald
Passing a razor over the head
And it was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית שמאי are saying 'just wave a razor and you are done'. According to רבי אבינא they mean the opposite: the requirement stands, and he cannot fulfill it.

phrases.english: Yes, and it was taught:
A completely bald nazir,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: צָרִיךְ הַעֲבָרַת תַּעַר,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: he must have a razor passed over,
and Beit Hillel say:
he does not need a razor passed over.
And Rabbi Avina said:
When Beit Shammai say 'must',
he must, and he has no remedy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the קשיא of step 8 by bringing a parallel case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel usage: the same word means the same thing in another ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'צריך' always means a requirement that can actually be carried out.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'צריך' can mean a requirement that cannot be fulfilled, so there is no remedy. That keeps רב חסדא's reading alive.

steps.title: רבי פדת reads בית שמאי differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי אבינא argues with רבי פדת. רבי פדת says בית שמאי and רבי אלעזר hold the same view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this argues with רבי פדת. For רבי פדת said: בית שמאי and רבי אלעזר said the same thing. בית שמאי's view is the one we just quoted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side point. Not everyone reads בית שמאי the way רבי אבינא does. This line sets up the source for רבי אלעזר in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פדת understands בית שמאי as saying: pass the razor over the bald head, and that counts as shaving. In his view, בית שמאי's 'צריך' means 'do it the closest way you can, and you are done'. It does not mean 'no remedy'.

keyTerms.meaning: And it argues with
The same thing (the same opinion)
That which we just said

phrases.english: And this argues with Rabbi Pedat.
For Rabbi Pedat said:
Beit Shammai and Rabbi Elazar
said the same thing.
Beit Shammai: that which we said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It shows that רבי אבינא's reading, used in step 9, is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי פדת, בית שמאי and רבי אלעזר share one view: you do the act in the closest possible way, and you fulfill your obligation.

steps.title: Source for רבי אלעזר: putting blood on the spot of a missing thumb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source for רבי אלעזר's view. It is about a מצורע who has no thumb or big toe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר's view comes from this teaching. If a מצורע has no thumb or big toe, he can never become pure. רבי אלעזר says: the כהן puts the blood on the spot where it would be, and that counts. רבי שמעון says: if he put it on the left side, that counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source that shows רבי אלעזר's view. This makes clear why רבי פדת compares him to בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says a missing body part means no purity ever. רבי אלעזר says you put the blood on the place where the thumb should be, and that works. That matches how רבי פדת reads בית שמאי: the razor goes over the bald head, and that works.

keyTerms.meaning: The thumb and the big toe
Purity ever / forever
He puts it on its place (where the limb would be)
He has fulfilled the obligation

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read 'צריך'. רבי אבינא reads it as 'he needs it but has no remedy'. רבי פדת reads it as 'do it the closest way, and you fulfill it', like רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, as it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ בּוֹהֶן יָד וּבוֹהֶן רֶגֶל —
phrases.english: If he has no thumb and no big toe,
he can never become pure.
Rabbi Elazar says:
He puts it on its place and fulfills the obligation.
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם נָתַן עַל שֶׁל שְׂמֹאל — יָצָא.
phrases.english: If he put it on the left one, he has fulfilled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It completes רבי פדת's statement by citing רבי אלעזר's source.
steps.raayaObject: רבי פדת's claim that בית שמאי and רבי אלעזר hold the same view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching about a מצורע without a thumb or big toe, where רבי אלעזר says to put the blood on its place.

steps.title: The blood for the מצורע is caught in the כהן's hand
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that the blood placed on the מצורע must be taken by the כהן's own hand, not in a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And he shall take from the blood of the אשם.' I might think he takes it in a כלי. So the פסוק says 'and he shall put'. Just as putting is done with the כהן's own body, so too taking is done with the כהן's own body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how the blood of the אשם מצורע is collected. It compares 'taking' to 'putting' in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן puts the blood on the מצורע with his own finger. The ברייתא learns that the taking must also be done with his body, so he catches the blood in his hand. This is a special rule for the blood that goes on the מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
One might have thought
Therefore the פסוק says
Taking (collecting the blood)
Putting (placing the blood)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'And he shall take from the blood of the guilt-offering',
one might think in a vessel;
therefore the verse says: 'and he shall put'.
Just as putting is with the priest's own body,
so too taking is with the priest's own body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It starts a new ברייתא, still about the אשם מצורע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood that goes on the מצורע is collected in the כהן's hand.

steps.title: The blood for the מזבח still needs a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the blood for the מזבח is also caught by hand. It answers no, because the אשם is compared to a חטאת, which needs a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might think the blood for the מזבח is also taken by hand. So the פסוק says 'for like the חטאת, so is the אשם'. Just as a חטאת needs a כלי, so too an אשם needs a כלי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא limits the hand rule from the last step. The blood for the מזבח must still be caught in a כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this פסוק, we might apply the hand rule to all the blood. The comparison to a חטאת teaches that the blood for the מזבח follows the normal rule and needs a כלי. So only the blood for the מצורע is the exception.

keyTerms.meaning: For like the חטאת, so is the אשם
Requires a vessel
The altar

phrases.english: One might think that even for the altar it is so;
therefore the verse says:
'For like the sin-offering, so is the guilt-offering'.
Just as a sin-offering requires a vessel,
so too a guilt-offering requires a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It limits the hand rule of step 12 to the blood for the מצורע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood of the אשם מצורע that goes on the מזבח must be caught in a כלי, like a חטאת.

steps.title: Two כהנים collect the blood: one by hand, one in a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that two כהנים catch the blood of the אשם מצורע. One catches it in a כלי for the מזבח, and one catches it by hand for the מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: So you find yourself saying: for the אשם מצורע, two כהנים catch its blood, one in his hand and one in a כלי. The one who caught it in the כלי goes to the מזבח. The one who caught it in his hand goes to the מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא puts its two rules together. It describes the practical result: two כהנים are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 requires a hand for the מצורע's blood, and step 13 requires a כלי for the מזבח's blood. Both must happen at the same time from the same animal. So two כהנים catch the blood together, each in his own way.

keyTerms.meaning: You find yourself saying (it turns out that)
The guilt-offering of a מצורע
Receive / collect its blood

steps.whatToRemember: The blood of the אשם מצורע is caught twice at once. One כהן uses a כלי for the מזבח, and another uses his hand for the מצורע's ear, thumb, and toe.

phrases.english: You find that you say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע שְׁנֵי כֹהֲנִים מְקַבְּלִים אֶת דָּמוֹ,
phrases.english: for the leper's guilt-offering, two priests collect its blood,
one by hand and one in a vessel.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁקִּבֵּל בִּכְלִי בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: The one who collected in a vessel goes to the altar,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה שֶׁקִּיבֵּל בַּיָּד בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל מְצוֹרָע.
phrases.english: and the one who collected by hand goes to the leper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It combines steps 12 and 13 into one practical procedure.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The אשם מצורע needs two כהנים: one catches the blood in a כלי for the מזבח, and one catches it in his hand for the מצורע.

steps.title: A משנה elsewhere: all the replaced animals are burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say every replaced animal makes garments impure and is burned at the בית הדשן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: All of them make garments impure and are burned at the place of the ashes. These are the words of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from another place. That משנה deals with the animals that were replaced because their blood spilled, and with what happens to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that if the blood spills partway through, a new animal is brought to finish the service. This משנה asks about the first animals that were set aside. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון treat all of them like a full inner חטאת. So the people who burn them become impure, and they are burned at the בית הדשן.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה in another place
They make the garments of the people who burn them impure
The place of the ashes, where inner חטאות are burned
They are burned

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishna):
And all of them render garments impure
phrases.notes: "All of them" means every animal whose blood spilled and was replaced.

phrases.english: and are burned at the place of the ashes,
the words of Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic. It moves from the catching of the אשם מצורע blood back to the animals of יום הכפורים whose blood spilled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, every replaced bull or goat makes garments impure and is burned at the בית הדשן.

steps.title: The חכמים: only the last animal is burned there
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree. Only the last animal makes garments impure and is burned at the בית הדשן, because it finished the כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: They do not make garments impure, and they are not burned at the place of the ashes. Only the last one is, since the atonement was finished with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposing view of the חכמים. They say only the final animal gets these laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים give a clear reason: the last animal is the one that finished the כפרה. The earlier animals were started but never finished the job. So they do not get the special laws of burning at the בית הדשן and making garments impure.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, meaning the majority view
The last one, the final animal brought
Since, because
The atonement was completed with it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say every replaced animal is burned at the בית הדשן. The חכמים say only the last one is, because only it completed the כפרה.
steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying the earlier animals stop being חטאות. They only say these two laws, burning at the בית הדשן and making garments impure, apply just to the animal that finished the כפרה.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
they do not render garments impure,
and they are not burned at the place of the ashes
except for the last one,
since atonement was completed with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view inside the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the final animal, which completed the כפרה, makes garments impure and is burned at the בית הדשן.

steps.title: רבא asks how many goats are sent away
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן how many goats are sent to עזאזל if new pairs of goats had to be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: How many goats does he send away?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a new question. If the blood of the inside goat spills, a new pair of goats is brought and a new lottery is held. That can leave more than one goat set aside for עזאזל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each new lottery picks one more goat for עזאזל. So after a few spills, there could be several עזאזל goats waiting. רבא wants to know whether all of them are sent away, or only one.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question)
Goats
He sends away (to עזאזל)
How many

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Naḥman:
How many goats does he send away?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, still about replacing animals whose blood spilled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When several goats were chosen for עזאזל because of repeated lotteries, how many of them are sent away?

steps.title: רב נחמן: Do you send a whole flock?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers sharply: does he send away his whole flock? Only one goat is sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Does he send away his whole flock?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers with a rhetorical question. He means it is obvious that only one goat is sent away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה describes sending one goat to עזאזל, not many. So רב נחמן says the question seems silly, as if someone would send away an entire flock. The extra goats are not sent.

keyTerms.meaning: And would...? (opens a rhetorical question)
His flock

phrases.english: He said to him:
And does he send away his flock?
phrases.notes: He's not really asking. Of course not! Only one goat is sent.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only one goat is sent to עזאזל. Sending all of them would be like sending a whole flock.

steps.title: רבא begins to explain his question
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts to answer רב נחמן. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבא is about to explain what he really meant, and his words continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן treated the question as obvious. Now רבא is about to make clear that he was asking something more precise. The content of his reply comes in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (here, רבא replies)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Here the speaker is רבא, replying to רב נחמן. His words continue on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא responds to רב נחמן's rhetorical answer, preparing to make his question more precise.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The setup for רבא's clarified question, which continues in the next section.
